fixes.explanation: Jesus doesn't point to the crowds here. He says, “The works I do in My Father’s name testify on My behalf.” The witness is what He does, not who is standing around. A big crowd is nice, but it isn't the answer.
Jesus actually does say it. His words are, “But because you are not My sheep, you refuse to believe.” So the statement is true, friend. They asked Him to tell them plainly, and I think He did.
Praise sounds lovely, but it isn't the word here. Jesus says, “My sheep listen to My voice; I know them, and they follow Me.” The word is follow. Listen, known, follow, friend.
Bowing isn't what the text shows, friend. It says, “At this, the Jews again picked up stones to stone Him.” Stones, not worship. It's a heavy moment.

Jesus does say it, friend. While talking about those to whom the word of God came, He says, “the Scripture cannot be broken.” So the statement is true. I'd keep that line close, because it's a sturdy one.

Moses, Israel's leader (Exodus 3:10), is a big name, but Jesus doesn't compare Himself to him here. He says, “How then can you accuse Me of blasphemy for stating that I am the Son of God?” He calls Himself the Son of God. That's the claim they accuse Him over.

David, Israel's king (1 Samuel 16:13), is a great name, but Jesus doesn't use it here. He says, “How then can you accuse Me of blasphemy for stating that I am the Son of God?” The title He names is Son of God, friend.
John it is. Jesus goes back across the Jordan to the place where John had first been baptizing, and He stays there. Friend, that's a quiet landing spot after all that grabbing in Jerusalem.
Peter is a good name to know, but the text doesn't connect him to this place. It says Jesus went to the place where John had first been baptizing. So the name we want is John, friend.

All true. The people say, “Although John never performed a sign, everything he said about this man was true.” No signs, but his words held up. Friend, I'd love to be that dependable when I say a batch will be ready in ten minutes.
Telling Him to leave isn't what the text says, friend. It says, “Many came to Him…” and then, “And many in that place believed in Jesus.” They come to Him, and they believe. That's the ending.
